work_completed: Created Rust crate crates/nlt-toi (Cargo.toml + src/lib.rs) implementing RFC 8785 JCS canonicalization ported from the TS reference (packages/toi/src/canonicalize.ts) and Python reference (src/nlt_toi/canonicalize.py).

Implemented full ECMA-262 Number::toString (6.1.6.1.20) on top of ryu shortest digits — ryu alone emits 42.0/1e-6/1e7 which is not JCS-conformant; implemented decimal vs exponential selection exactly as the Python _format_number reference (including 1e+21 form).
post_process_numbers rewrites serde_json's ryu float output to JCS form while passing integer tokens through verbatim so i64/u64 beyond 2^53 keep exact precision.
Added 17 Rust tests incl. 9 cross-runtime parity vectors ported verbatim from the TS and Python known-answer suites — all green (cargo test).
Re-verified Python reference baseline: tests/test_canonicalize.py 10 passed.
Committed [OpenCode CTO Orchestrator] feat(nlt-toi): Rust JCS canonicalizer (RFC 8785) and opened PR #24 on branch rust/nlt-toi-jcs-canonicalizer.
work_in_progress: Go JCS canonicalizer (Phase 0 Task 2) not started — at go/nlt-toi/ per the port plan.
decisions_made: Deliver the Rust port as a Rust workspace member crates/nlt-toi rather than a top-level rust/ tree, to mirror the Python src/ layout and allow per-pillar crates.
format_number follows ECMA-262 exactly (1e+21 with plus sign), matching JS String(1e21) and the Python reference — NOT the ryu default.
Integers pass through post-processing un-parsed to preserve precision beyond 2^53.
handoff_record.next_agent_notes: Build the Go JCS canonicalizer at go/nlt-toi/ using json.Decoder.UseNumber() and the same known-answer vectors (they are in crates/nlt-toi/src/lib.rs cross_runtime_parity module). Then validate all three implementations (TS, Python, Rust, Go) against a shared vector corpus before Phase 1 (core types + Ed25519 signing). Run nlt-code-reviewer at each phase gate.
